scope: Research packet for parent integration. New candidate book pages are nomination sources; broad catalogues and reviews are scouting or verification sources. No assertion that every title mentioned in those broader pages was formally nominated or that all their comments were collected.
score_profile: E20, S17 and D10 quadratic; U15 M12 R9 F7 A5 N3 P2 linear. Raw assessments formed before score calculation. Amazon final records are parent-owned; this file does not substitute Goodreads/StoryGraph/LibraryThing counts for Amazon.
confidence: Moderate book-level judgments from publisher excerpts/contents and independent reviews; high bibliographic confidence unless noted.

platform_strategy.use: Locate comparable books and read opposing substantive reviews for recurrent fit, repetition, coherence or accuracy issues. Search exact title and author; disambiguate works and editions.
platform_strategy.limitation: Average stars and total ratings reflect self-selected audiences and are not accuracy scores. Edition and cache snapshots differ. Neither count can supply rule 15.

platform_strategy.use: Prefer identified engineers or specialist scholars explaining a mechanism, limitation, or reason for their choice. Follow the specific book's publisher page for nomination.
platform_strategy.limitation: The AI category also lists recommendations generated by ChatGPT; these are not independent expert votes. An engineer's popular introduction can remain too elementary for this user. Distinguish fivebooks.com from similarly named sites.

platform_strategy.use: Use awards to discover clear explanatory narrative, then use named specialist reviews to challenge central claims. For institutional science, the actual Frontiers review of Science Fictions was more diagnostic than the prize nomination.
platform_strategy.limitation: Prize selection is broad and does not establish this user's thematic fit; several shortlists emphasize health or environment. Publisher blurbs copied across booksellers count as one source, not independent convergence.

platform_strategy.use: Seek technical readers who inspect failure modes and counterarguments. The Alignment Forum reviews directly tested Christian's treatment of COMPAS objections, incentives and learning methods.
platform_strategy.limitation: Do not transfer a reviewer's separate mistaken claim into the book. Discussion votes are not independent quality observations.

search_filters.eligibility: General explanatory narrative or sustained argument; central computing/engineering/production/scientific organization; no primary instruction or specialist reference.
search_filters.high_yield: Prefer original years 2000 onward, no T11/T12, no bounded old historical endpoint, and likely Amazon >=1000. These are discovery priorities, not new exclusion rules.
search_filters.deduction_bound: A title with any -10 thematic deduction cannot exceed 92, since positive maxima sum to 100. With O15=-5 a 2020 title requires positive >97.60, which is possible but demanding. A 2023 title with O15=0 requires positive >92.30.
search_filters.content_bound: The quadratic evidence, integration and density criteria make depth plus synthesis critical. A narrow excellent introduction need not be an exceptional overall fit.
search_filters.not_a_probability_model: No calibrated probability or expected score is asserted. Search ordering follows algebraic feasibility and observed content signals.

candidates.title: The Alignment Problem: Machine Learning and Human Values
candidates.author: Brian Christian

parent_amazon_observation.provenance: Parent independently verified identified US hardcover/paperback and UK paperback; 716 was the largest single matching aggregate observed. Parent owns exact marketplace/product/date record.

candidates.eligibility: Three-part explanatory narrative about machine learning representation, learning and alignment. Historical and biographical scenes support mechanisms; no course, exercises or procedural training structure. Bias and law are application cases, not a political manifesto. Computing remains central.

criterion_notes.E: Strong documentation and explicit opposing cases; sampled technical readers found key objections addressed. Not every empirical claim independently audited.
criterion_notes.S: Links machine learning, neuroscience, behavior, institutional decisions and law. Production/trade/industrial scaling are secondary.
criterion_notes.U: General lessons in proxy optimization, specification, feedback, distribution shift and uncertainty.
criterion_notes.M: Explains why learning systems fail and how proposed fixes work, including their limits.
criterion_notes.D: Substantive 329-page text within a longer volume of notes; some biography reduces maximum density.
criterion_notes.R: Enduring specification problems; frontier implementations and proposed solutions age.
criterion_notes.A: Unusual synthesis survived substantive technical attention; full score does not mean the author is a leading algorithm inventor.

Perceptron training, representations, proxy objectives and counterarguments in fairness examples.
Three-part contents and technically informed positive assessment; some connections left implicit.

hard_exclusion_recommendations.title: Algorithms to Live By: The Computer Science of Human Decisions
hard_exclusion_recommendations.reason: The introduction expressly promises practical suggestions for specific everyday problems. Eleven chapters are organized as methods to apply: optimal stopping, exploration, sorting, caching, scheduling, Bayes, overfitting, relaxation, randomness, networking and game theory. Under the repository's strict primary-purpose test, this is a mixed conceptual narrative whose main organizing purpose remains applying methods.
hard_exclusion_recommendations.counterargument: Strong explanatory computer-science narrative and accessible history; no classroom exercises. This makes classification less clear than a textbook. Parent should resolve consistently with comparable previous exclusions. Do not infer exclusion merely from the word Algorithms.

sources.supports: Authorized introduction and stated practical aims.
Publisher-supplied contents and chapter excerpt.
Russ Allbery review separates interesting CS ideas from less persuasive practical advice.
